rationale: Replace find_frame's per-id glob over frames/*/<id>.jsonl with one process-local id -> path table built by a single scandir pass, keeping the returned value identical to what the same-moment glob would return. On the live ledger (5881 frames) lineage-show spends most of its time in find_frame; the table takes the warm run from 32.4 s to 11.4 s with byte-identical stdout. Three obligations preserve the contract: a vanished indexed path falls back to glob, any append under frames/ in this process invalidates the table, and multiple live matches still raise. One residual difference is disclosed rather than hidden: a second file created for an already-indexed id by another process is not seen until the table is rebuilt.
rollback_triggers: candidate changes any file outside the two declared candidate paths
find_frame returns a path the same-moment glob would not have returned
a frame opened by the running process becomes invisible to a later lookup in that process
the duplicate-id RuntimeError or the missing-id FileNotFoundError stops being raised
lineage-show stdout stops being byte-identical between baseline and candidate on the same ledger
any test passing on the baseline fails on the candidate
the disclosed foreign-second-file race widens beyond a single already-indexed id
installed Skill, evaluation authority, adoption state, or deployment state changes without an independent cosigned adoption decision
